motif: A silvered hollow crescent (Prata Oxidada) cut or hung into every roofline or crown, with one small Ametista de Véspera glass lens seated in its hollow; the crescent is the trim, the lens is the only saturated accent.

buildings.colour: weathered ochre canvas over grey spoil
buildings.why: Chain top of Hunter's Hall, so it keeps the long low shed and grows it into a dug-in den under a spoil-heap roof, with one banner pole. Ochre canvas is shared with the chain.
A railway signal mast is the tallest thin vertical in the race, and the dish and lantern make a clear top. Grey iron stands apart from the ochre neighbour.
A settling basin cut into the ground reads as a hole, and the iridescent oil is the only bright spot. The dark stone contrasts with the iron before it.
Keeps the chain's leaning mass and grows it into three misaligned crate-board floors that lean off-axis, with shuttered ports instead of windows.

buildings.colour: bone-white dead wood with oiled canvas hood
buildings.why: A lean-to against a dead tree is a single sloped mass. The bone-white tree crown separates it from the dark Guild next to it.
Base of the chain, a wide low shed with a two-pitch tarpaulin roof. Ochre sits beside bone-white and rust, so it separates from both.

buildings.colour: rust-red chained iron on pale slab
buildings.why: Chain top of the Moon Shrine: the ring of the shrine's plates grows into a slab with a central post and chained machinery. Rust red separates it from the plum shrine.
A split drum laid on its side and ringed by tilted plates forms a hollow crown. The Véspera plum body ties it to the race palette.

buildings.colour: clay-brown earth berm with galvanised sheet
buildings.why: A half-buried semicircular berm is a low dome, and the leaning derrick is a small spike on top of it. Earth brown differs from plum.
A monolith made of stacked kerb slabs reads as terraces, with a silver spiral inlay. Pale stone is the lightest body in the race.
The exposed rib beams and the one standing wall form openings you can see through. Black char sits beside pale limestone.
Keeps the Hunter's Hall shed and grows it with a continuous upper gallery on silver crescents. Ochre canvas follows the chain, and it is next to black char, not ochre.
Chain top of the Pillaged Hut: a single standing gable with a crescent-shaped hole that you can see through is a bigger pierced arch. Brick red separates it from the charcoal hut and the ochre hall.

buildings.colour: pale silvered birch wood with clear glass jars
buildings.why: A round bank of stumps and full condenser jars forms a drum of glass, and the filled jars show the stacks. Pale birch is a different hue from brick red.

buildings.archetype: spired cluster of two or three peaks
buildings.why: The cracked derrick bit and its two or three shards make a jagged crown of peaks. Oil black differs from pale birch, and the amethyst lens sits in its crown.
